coverage.row: An ancestor kill of a realm that hosts a nested Worker, while that realm is busy, retires every nested thread (ADR-0548 Proof: RED with 21 Workers retained, then green)
IpcFrame control:kill-tree requires a boolean cascade; the process shim refuses a missing or non-boolean bit with a loud control:self-exit 1
WorkerProcessHandle.controlKill(pid, signal, cascade): the sender sets cascade=true when the route's physical owner or one of its tree ancestors has an admitted kill, and false for a live host
ProcessManager.kill(pid, signal, realmEnding) latches the manager one-way. Later frames carry cascade=true, and every later physical end is release() without terminate()
SpawnWorkerResult.release(): closes input, detaches the ring, removes listeners, keeps the error guard, never calls terminate()
coverage.note: Most of the clause is now discriminated: no terminate(), ring detach, and only the error listener left (mutant H, which keeps lifecycle listeners, fails). 'Input closed' is still not: mutant I (release skips inputBinding.dispose()) passes all 296 kernel tests. See the Bugs concern on release().

coverage.row: A live realm (owner root, or a parent that outlives its killed child) still calls terminate() at once
The bound descendant authority kill(pid, signal, realmEnding) receives the frame's cascade bit
SpawnOptions.remoteControl.kill(pid, signal, cascade): the no-COI sender forwards cascade on its kill-tree frame
coverage.note: No carrier tests the frame contents. Mutant C (cascade:false) still passes. In no-COI realms the bit has no behavioral effect: their children are raw Workers (child_process.ts:389), and the cleanup terminate() ignores the latch. Reception recorded this as NOTE in the residuals. See the Bugs concern on no-COI.
